rows.feature: build time of one primitive (the whole page waits for it)
rows.evidence: MEASURED, one SolidCraft call = build + measure as ONE SYNCHRONOUS wasm call that does not yield (referee wrapper solidcraft_referee.run; it cannot be split into build and measure here, so the cost of the measure tessellation is inside these numbers). Median wall time of 3 runs through the guard on a 24-core machine whose load average was 14-51 during the run (cpu time ~ wall time, so this is real compute, inflated by contention): box 14 ms; cone 26 ms; prism7 3 ms; wedge 2 ms; cyl 420 ms; box-corner 2.7 s; sph 3.7 s; ring 17 s; cyl-corner 16 s; cyl-chamfer 585 ms. Wider ranges over the sweeps: plain box/prism/wedge 3-80 ms; cone 25-480 ms; cylinder 0.2-9 s (needle to 1e6 wide); rounded box 2.1 s median over E1 (max 5.8 s); cylinder corner 14 s median, up to 56 s (bevel 981 ms, up to 10.0 s); sphere 215 ms to 16 s (median 2.3 s; from across 2 up to 6e4 it is 4-16 s whatever the size, only the tiny ones are faster); ring 4.4 s to 69 s (median 21 s), size does not matter. Load changes these by 2-4x (the same sphere took 4.2 s and 13.9 s in two runs minutes apart), so quote them as orders of magnitude. WHAT THE PAGE MUST DO (a requirement, not measured here: the rig has no browser): run the SolidCraft call in a Web Worker, never on the main thread, because a sphere, a ring or a rounded cylinder blocks the thread for seconds to a minute; show a building state; give every call a time budget (suggest 120 s: the slowest supported call measured was 69 s, so the budget leaves about 1.7x headroom) and terminate the worker when it runs out, with the sentence "<call>: building took too long and was stopped -- try a smaller or simpler shape." The size caps in the rows above already remove the known minute-and-more cases (ring(1e5): 52-92 s, correct volume).

rows.feature: independent (non-OCCT) check of wedge orientation and prism vertex phase
rows.evidence: NOT MEASURED, reason: no FreeCAD reference covers any primitive feature. The 218 saved FreeCAD results under docs/replica/freecad/gauntlet/variants/refs contain no Part primitive (box/cylinder/sphere/cone/torus/prism/wedge): 0 of 218. The five refs used in the rows above (ref-pad-basic__thin-plate, __slender-post, __circle-offcentre, __hexagon, ref-revolution__top-solid-rod) are Pad / Revolution results of a sketch, compared as the same solid (volume, bbox, COM, face count): they cover box, cylinder and a hexagonal prism but are not primitive features. Consequences: (1) the wedge claim (right triangle with legs along +x and +y from the corner, extruded along z, centred on the bounding box; FreeCAD PartDesign::Wedge is a different parametrisation) rests on live OCCT, i.e. on packages/brep-adapter occt-build, which is the same code that DEFINES the ModelDoc semantics, so it is not an independent check of the meaning; truck, OCCT, brep-rs and the closed form w*d*h/2 agree on the volume but they could all be built on the same misreading of the orientation. brep-rs, built from the same ModelDoc spec, agrees as well and is no more independent. (2) The prism vertex phase (first vertex at angle 0, circumradius across/2) is checked against FreeCAD only for n = 6 (the hexagon Pad ref: bbox equal, dVol 1.8e-11); for n = 3, 5, 7, 12 it rests on occt-build. (3) Ring, sphere and cone have closed forms (2 pi^2 R r^2, 4/3 pi r^3, pi r^2 h / 3) that are independent of every kernel and were used as the third oracle for every curved row.

rows.feature: pre-flight envelope (every limit in one place) and its regression proof
rows.evidence: ONE guard replaces the scattered per-row limits (contract/primitives.guard.mjs LIM): box corner <= half the shortest side x (1 - 0.0001); cylinder corner/bevel <= 0.99 x radius and <= half the height x (1 - 0.0001); ring across/tubeAcross in [2.05, 50] and tubeAcross >= 0.5; curved or rounded shapes: every typed size <= 50000, across (shortest side for a rounded box) >= 1, tall >= 0.01; planar shapes: every size in [0.001, 1000000]; cylinder tall <= 30 x across, cone tall <= 40 x across; |at| <= 1000000; curved: |at| <= 400 x smallest size; prism and turned shapes: |at| <= 100 x smallest size; box chamfer style refused; script text: no surplus value after the options object, whole-number prism sides, no cone second radius. PROOF 1, over everything ever measured for this group (primitives.guard-check.mjs, 1410 distinct inputs from 119 result files): truck built a WRONG solid (volume, bbox, COM or face count outside the bars) for 432 of them and the guard refuses 432 of 432, ACCEPTS 0; 0 accepted inputs built a solid that no oracle could check (11 such inputs are refused); the guard accepts 671 inputs that truck builds correctly and refuses 192 that truck builds correctly (conservative edge bands: exactly-half corners, 5e4-1e6 cylinders, 0.5-1 mm shapes, planar ratios 100-200, curved ratios 400-1000, thin and fat rings, slender cylinders/cones 30-50). 103 inputs that truck or the interpreter already refused are given a plain sentence instead of kernel text. Every guard sentence passes the lint (starts with the call the student typed, no internal id such as box1, no kernel word such as solid.fillet / major / minor): 0 problems. PROOF 2, end to end through the rig with the guard in front of the translator: the 47 supported representatives (3 runs each, 141 runs) all build and match the oracle (primitives-regress-check.mjs g1: 0 failing), and the 91 refused representatives all come back guard-refused with the expected code and a lint-clean sentence (g2: 0 failing); the same 89 inputs without the guard: 47 wrong solids with status built, 24 refusals in kernel text, 16 correct solids that the guard refuses on purpose (edge bands, silent script changes), 2 interpreter refusals. See contract/primitives-r3/results/regress-summary.txt for every before/after pair. STILL OPEN (not claimed as supported): the guard is a prototype outside packages/script; the Worker and time-budget behaviour is a requirement; a primitive moved by a move() feature is folded back in for the placement rules, but a primitive that is repeated, mirrored or booleaned goes through those groups.
